description: Single source of truth for the MARS+ EVA model. Read by pipeline/ (C#) and app/ (JS).

walking.source: Tobler (1993) hiking function scaled x0.5 for a pressurized suit: ~2.5 km/h on flat ground (scenario assumption)

pace.source: Travel-time multipliers for crew pace (scenario assumption)

sources.slope: HiRISE 1 m DTM (USGS Mars 2020 TRN); cells steeper than 20 deg are blocked (scenario assumption)
sources.sand: Walking on sand costs 2.1-2.7x the energy of firm ground (Lejeune et al. 1998, J. Exp. Biol. 201:2071); aeolian units from Stack et al. 2020
sources.rocks: Shadow fraction in the 25 cm HiRISE orthoimage (shadow-based rock detection principle, Golombek et al.)

workspace.source: Suited work area next to the rover stops: slope <= 10 deg and large-dune fraction <= 0.5 (both inclusive), and no blocked cell. Scenario assumption, searched around the Robine and Malay rover positions.

sensitivity.source: Walking-time multiplier on large aeolian bedforms tested around the model value (x2); the energy cost of walking on sand is 2.1-2.7x firm ground (Lejeune et al. 1998)

eva.source: Scenario assumptions for the pilot; adjustable in the app

weather.source: Scenario thresholds applied to MEDA ground temperature and mean wind (Perseverance, sols 286-339)

radiation.source: MSL RAD dose rate (Gale crater), Oct 2021; Jezero is higher than Gale so local dose would be somewhat larger. Nominal dose is the background rate times time on the surface (walking + tasks). Airlock time is inside the habitat and the reserve is unused margin, so neither counts as exposure.

dust.source: Postpone the EVA when Mastcam-Z 880 nm column optical depth is at least 1.0. In sols 286-339 the non-storm daily medians stay at or below 0.845 (median about 0.50) and the highest storm-day median is 1.376 (sols 316-317; sol 313 has no Mastcam-Z tau in the table). Lemmon et al. 2022 (doi:10.1029/2022GL100126) separately report an RDS visible peak near 1.7; that peak is not a row in the Mastcam-Z table (doi:10.17632/gktjp9jptb.2) and is not used as a measurement. Typical and worst weather share the background dust value: worst refers to temperature and wind. The 1.0 threshold is a scenario rule for this planner.

visibility.source: Scenario assumption for geometric line of sight only, not a radio model. The habitat antenna is 3 m above the local surface and the crew eye is 1.5 m (values from Henry's line-of-sight prototype). Used to prefer return routes that keep the habitat in view during a dust storm.

contingency.source: Emergency return during the EVA. A dust storm or a solar particle event cannot be avoided by rerouting inside the 1 km2 pilot area, so the planner gives the way back to the habitat (the only shelter). SCENARIO ASSUMPTIONS, pending the science team: return checkpoints every 5 min and at each stop; the particle-event dose uses the peak RAD rate of 28 Oct 2021 (detector E, Gale; conservative); dust-safe route blocks slopes above 15 deg (normal limit 20), weighs large dunes x(1+2*fraction) and cells without line of sight to the habitat x1.25 when choosing the route, and is walked 1.5x slower for low visibility; warn when any point of the plan is more than 45 min from the habitat. The warning never changes the recommended plan. How much warning an alert gives on Mars is not known and is not modelled.
